title: RISE-VR Prevent
summary:
Adolescence is a vulnerable phase for young people. Mental health conditions such as anxiety disorders and depression are the most common mental health conditions among adolescents.
Only a few of them take advantage of (professional) services; reasons for this include a lack of available services and long wait times.
There is therefore a great need for accessible interventions that require as few therapists as possible.
One possibility for this could be the use of  virtual reality (VR) applications. These could be used to strengthen adolescents’ skills in the areas of resilience, introspection, emotion regulation, and social interaction in order to equip them with the skills they need to
protect themselves from potential long-term consequences.

The study is primarily designed to answer the following questions:
1.) Does the intervention via a remote VR application, when
compared to the waiting-list control group, lead to a significant
reduction in symptoms of depression and/or anxiety?
2.) When used as an adjunct to therapy, can the VR application
contribute to a further significant reduction in
depression and/or anxiety symptoms?
3.) Can VR be successfully integrated
into existing psychotherapies?

This is an intervention. As part of the
project, two studies (RISE Treat and RISE Prevent) are being conducted with a total of four groups. The four groups are: a waiting-list control group, psychotherapy only, and
VR, and VR+Psychotherapy. The two VR groups receive the
intervention over 12 weeks. It consists of
a maximum of 9 modules. The content covers resilience, introspection,
emotion regulation, and social skills.
All participants complete an
online questionnaire at three measurement time points: at the beginning, after 12 weeks, and
after 18 weeks. The online questionnaire consists of
standardized questionnaires that measure, among other things, depression, anxiety disorders, and emotion regulation, and is supplemented by other methods such as the collection of speech data.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At least mild symptoms of depression or anxiety disorders
At least a good command of German at the B2 level
Exclusion criteria:
Severe visual or hearing impairments
Epilepsy
Severe physical disabilities
Severe motion sickness
Acute Suicidal Tendencies
